findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact wording/placement of the seeded 'already credited — do not re-verify' directive AND add a co-located system-prompt rule teaching the primary how to honor a seeded/credited annotation, rather than relying on the documented-as-untrusted data-only manifest channel.
evidence: completion_banking.py:199-201: manifest 'appended to the primary's untrusted ticket context; the authoritative banking instructions remain in the system prompt'

Plan 3(b): 'since the manifest is data-only, the primary context ALSO annotates each seeded criterion's prose with an "already credited — do not re-verify" directive, so the primary ... actually skips them'

ABSENCE: the plan does not add a corresponding system-prompt decision rule instructing the model that a seeded/credited annotation may appear in ticket context and must be honored; the directive-processing protocol is not co-located with the authoritative-instruction surface (T8(b)).
findings.finding: The plan injects a new imperative behavioral directive ('already credited — do not re-verify') into the primary verifier's UNTRUSTED, data-only ticket context (the primary_criteria_manifest channel), whose docstring states authoritative instructions live only in the system prompt — an instruction-locality antipattern, and the plan never specifies a co-located system-prompt rule that tells the primary how to interpret a seeded/credited annotation.
findings.location: Plan step 3(b) and AC3 ('the primary context marks each seeded criterion "already credited — do not re-verify"')
scenarios: Primary verifier treats the credited annotation as untrusted ticket prose and re-verifies the seeded criterion anyway, burning the very budget the cache is meant to conserve.
The pink-elephant effect: listing a seeded criterion and telling the model not to touch it draws attention to it.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the authoritative 'skip credited criteria' instruction into the primary's system prompt (where banking instructions already live), and keep only a neutral data marker (e.g. a `seeded`/`credited` field per manifest line) in the untrusted context; the system prompt references that field as the trusted signal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the exact field set persisted in a cached PASS record (and how evidence_sufficient/unverified/exhausted markers are re-derived on seed) so the seeded record shape matches what merge_finalizer_with_bank consumes.
evidence: completion_verdict_assembly.py:171-196: merge keys on record fields including evidence_sufficient (_restamp_marker), unverified, exhausted
Plan step 3: 'Cache entries store the FULL banked record (met, evidence, citations)' — enumerates only three fields

Plan step 3: '(Marker semantics from 1d71-a76c: cached entries are PASS-only; insufficiency never cached.)' establishes PASS-only but does not enumerate the persisted field set that seeding must reconstruct for merge.
findings.finding: The cross-run cached verdict record and its new seeded:true flag are consumed by the merge protocol, but the plan does not fully specify the record's schema vocabulary at the finalize/cache-write boundary — it says entries store 'the FULL banked record (met, evidence, citations)' yet the run bank's records also carry marker/insufficiency fields (evidence_sufficient, unverified, exhausted) that merge_finalizer_with_bank keys on; which of these are persisted vs. re-derived on seed is left ambiguous.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('Cache entries store the FULL banked record (met, evidence, citations)') and merge_finalizer_with_bank interaction
scenarios: A seeded record lacking the evidence_sufficient marker (or carrying a stale one) flows into merge_finalizer_with_bank and is re-stamped inconsistently, or a seeded record's field shape diverges from the run-bank record shape the merge path expects.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define a RETIRE/cleanup path for the completion_verdicts cache (e.g. prune entries whose criterion-hash is absent from the current ticket's criteria at finalize, or a TTL/max-entries eviction) so stale/superseded <criterion-hash>.json files do not accumulate indefinitely.
evidence: "Cache at .rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json, written ONLY on a validated PASS at finalize"
key each entry by (criterion-text hash, scoped content fingerprint) — a text or fingerprint change creates a NEW hash file, orphaning the old
No eviction, TTL, or cleanup mechanism is described for stale/superseded entries
findings.finding: The new ticket-scoped verdict cache (.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json) has a defined CREATE (write-on-PASS) and CONSUME (seed-at-run-start) path but NO RETIRE/cleanup path — as criterion text or scoped fingerprints rotate, superseded <criterion-hash>.json entries are never removed and accumulate indefinitely on disk.
scenarios: A ticket's criterion text is edited repeatedly across re-verifies, leaving one orphaned hash file per edit
A file under file_impact changes many times, rotating the fingerprint and leaving stale entries that never invalidate-and-delete
findings.suggested_fix: At finalize (or run start), after computing the current criteria set, delete any <criterion-hash>.json under the ticket dir whose hash is not in the current criteria manifest; add a test asserting orphaned entries are pruned.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In plan step 3, name the existing plan-review verdict-reuse mechanism (_idempotent_reuse/verdict_reuse, keyed on material_fingerprint + verified_at_sha) as prior art and state whether the new completion verdict cache deliberately diverges (per-blob scoping) or should share invalidation primitives.
evidence: Plan engages _resolve_tree_sha, BankStamps.material_fingerprint, and CriterionBank as prior art but omits the closest analogue: the plan-review PASS/BLOCK verdict-reuse paths keyed on material_fingerprint AND verified_at_sha
test_plan_review_reuse.py: '_idempotent_reuse (feature b3e5) covers only PASS ... its material_fingerprint AND verified_at_sha both still match'
findings.finding: The new cross-run PASS-verdict cache is a granular sibling of the repo's EXISTING plan-review verdict-reuse mechanism (_idempotent_reuse for PASS / verdict_reuse for BLOCK, keyed on material_fingerprint + verified_at_sha), but the plan neither names that prior art nor states how the new fingerprint/invalidation semantics align with or deliberately diverge from it — risking two divergent verdict-reuse idioms in one codebase.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (Cross-run PASS-verdict cache); prior art: tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review reuse paths
scenarios: A future maintainer must reconcile completion verdict caching with plan-review verdict reuse and finds two independently-evolved fingerprint schemes

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State an explicit back-out for the cross-run crediting behavior (e.g. a config flag that disables cache seeding / reverts merge to preserve-finalizer semantics), or justify that config-default revert alone is sufficient reversibility.
evidence: "this plan SCOPES A CHANGE: seeded: true records bypass finalizer judgment — an echo (incl. a met:false downgrade) is replaced by the bank's validated-PASS record"
This changes an existing preservation guarantee (finalizer's met on echoed records); no rollback/expand-contract statement accompanies the behavior change
findings.finding: The plan scopes a behavior change to merge_finalizer_with_bank (seeded records bypass finalizer judgment) and raises defaults that alter verifier outcomes, but states no explicit rollback/back-out mechanism for the new merge semantics or the persistent cache should the credited-verdict path prove unsafe.
scenarios: A cached PASS is later discovered to be a false-positive credit and operators need to disable cross-run crediting without a code revert
findings.suggested_fix: Add a boolean VerifyConfig key (e.g. completion_verify_cross_run_cache_enabled, default true) that, when false, disables seeding and restores the original merge_finalizer_with_bank semantics — providing a config-only kill-switch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In plan step 3, address the 6e4f prior-art lesson: state whether/how the completion verdict cache invalidates a cached PASS when the ticket's criteria-set membership or type changes (not just when a criterion's own text changes), and add a RED->GREEN test for it.
evidence: test_plan_review_reuse_type.py:1-7: 'Retyping a ticket must invalidate a reused plan-review verdict ... Both reuse paths gated only on the material fingerprint, which does not move when the type changes.'
Plan invalidation clause covers file-blob and criterion-text changes but is silent on ticket-type / criteria-set change
findings.finding: Prior art (ticket 6e4f) established that a fingerprint-only reuse key is unsafe across a change to which criteria APPLY: a reused verdict must also invalidate when the ticket type / criteria-set changes, because type selects criteria applicability. The plan keys cache entries only on (criterion-text hash, scoped content fingerprint) and lists no invalidation trigger for a change in the ticket's criteria-set membership or type, re-exposing the exact bug class the analogous prior art already fixed.
findings.location: Plan step 3, 'key each entry by (criterion-text hash, scoped content fingerprint)'; prior art: tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse_type.py (ticket 6e4f)
scenarios: A ticket is retyped or its criteria set is edited (a criterion removed/added) after a cached PASS; per-criterion text hashes for surviving criteria still match, so a stale PASS is seeded and credited

"Exhaustion converges across runs" is the goal, yet no observability of seed/hit/invalidation is planned to confirm it in production
findings.finding: The plan adds a new persistent write path (cache write-on-PASS) and new failure points (git rev-parse for fingerprints, child enumeration) with fail-open handling, but does not instrument cache hits/misses, seed events, or fingerprint-invalidations with a metric/log so operators can observe whether cross-run crediting is actually converging exhaustion (the stated goal).

A fingerprint bug silently invalidates every entry, defeating the cache with no visible signal

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify write-protection for seeded PASS records so the primary/successor cannot overwrite them before the finalizer merge (e.g. reject record_criterion_verdict upserts on seeded ids, or hold the validated PASS in a separate immutable structure the merge consults rather than the mutable provisional bank), and add a RED test where the primary banks met=false on a seeded id yet the credited PASS survives.
evidence: merge reads `entry = bank_entries.get(ids[text])` (completion_verdict_assembly.py:170) — the seeded record's durability depends on the bank not being overwritten

the record tool is `bank.make_record_tool()` (completion_tool_policy.py:102), an idempotent upsert keyed by criterion_id per CriterionBank docstring ('an idempotent upsert overwrites a prior provisional entry', completion_banking.py:405)
the plan's seeded-bypass is scoped to the finalizer echo/omission only ('seeded: true records bypass finalizer judgment'), not to bank writes
banked_ids/_first_unbanked (completion_tool_policy.py:113,144) skip seeded ids as WORK targets but do not block an explicit record call on a seeded id
findings.finding: The cross-run cache credits seeded PASS records only via a finalizer-merge bypass, but merge_finalizer_with_bank reads the substitute record from the same run-scoped bank the primary can overwrite; a seeded PASS is unprotected against an idempotent record_criterion_verdict upsert on its criterion_id by the primary (if it ignores the prose 'do not re-verify' directive) or a successor, silently degrading the credited verdict before finalize.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (seeding into run-scoped CriterionBank; merge_finalizer_with_bank interaction) / completion_verdict_assembly.py:170, completion_tool_policy.py:102
scenarios: primary LLM ignores the 'already credited' prose directive and banks a met=false on a seeded criterion, overwriting the validated-PASS bank record before finalize
a successor run banks over a seeded id
